topics.topic: Whether stop_required forces the recorded outcome to SandboxOutcome.CRASHED
questions: When stop_required is true but SandboxResult.outcome is not crashed, must the recorded outcome be forced to crashed, or must it remain the outcome corresponding to SandboxResult.outcome?
Must a stop_required result always have SandboxOutcome.CRASHED, or must execute_trial_case override a non-crashed sandbox outcome to crashed despite the same-name outcome rule?
Must a stop_required result always have SandboxOutcome.CRASHED, must execute_trial_case override any reported outcome to crashed, or must the requirement to record a crashed outcome change?

quotes: - execute_trial_case: [BEHAVIOR] MUST trust the writer invariant that every member of TrialCase.expected_outputs, when present, is a StoredValuesRef: add_trial_case is its only writer and stores every authored expected value or file fixture as such refs, while a captured case has expected_outputs None. The outcome is the sandbox outcome of the same name; a succeeded execution is passed when the case has no expected outputs or every output's digest equals the expected one — every digest compared is content_identity of a BytesContent holding the bytes: a value output's its canonical bytes, a file output's the bytes of its FilePayload content or of each FileListPayload contents item in list order — the same digest its FileFacts later records as content_digest —, both computed from what the sandbox returned, and an expected output's the value_digest of its StoredValue, read with read_records, for a value and for each file alike; the outcome is decided before any output is written, so no output is read back from the store —, a many file output equal only with the same length and equal digests position by position, and output_mismatch otherwise; a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant makes the outcome contract_violation.

- execute_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] When the SandboxResult reports stop_required, the execution is recorded first with its crashed outcome and detail_code, and then StopRequiredError is raised so that nothing further runs in the request; this capability does not infer stop from detail_code.
judgement.why: The same-name outcome rule preserves a non-crashed sandbox outcome, while the stop_required rule requires the recorded outcome to be crashed.

Must NotPermittedError be added to IMPORTS or MODULE-LOCAL EXCEPTION EXPORTS, or must answer_request raise an available imported exception instead?

quotes: the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else raise NotPermittedError; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1).
from cabinet_kernel.store import InvalidRequestError, RefusedError, StoreInternalError, UnknownReferenceError, open_store, page_records, read_records, read_value_bytes
Use only the IMPORTS listed above plus required standard library imports.
judgement.why: The requirement mandates raising NotPermittedError, but that name is neither imported nor permitted as a module-local exception.
